AES-128-GCM seal, 32 B, rind: 9 ns, 1.00× the fastest; verified: rind's Lean proof, through Aeneas and hand models of the function-pointer dispatch, the NEON transmutes, the one-pass short path, and the kernel dispatch Aeneas cannot translate, and of the NEON intrinsics as Arm's manual defines them, tested on an aarch64 CPU, of its AEAD API's AES-GCM key setup, seal, and open, for every AAD and message length it takes, down to its PMULL GHASH, its one-pass AES-GCM for short messages, and s2n-bignum's aes128_gcm_enc, aes128_gcm_dec, aes256_gcm_enc, and aes256_gcm_dec for the whole blocks of longer ones, and on cores with SHA3 their _alt forms, which rind runs only when the blocks' address plus their length is below 2^63, as their proofs require, against Vale's gcm_encrypt_LE and gcm_decrypt_LE, composed with s2n-bignum's HOL Light proofs of those kernels at 3f01260f and with rind's HOL Light proofs of its constant-time tag compare
